gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR adds a CSV export with an on-demand download button; you are its author, and robin and the team acme/reviewers are also requested reviewers. It covers CSV download and the header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, deliberately buffers the whole CSV instead of streaming it, and leaves the export screen to acme/export-ui.

Two problems must be fixed before this can merge.

1. The exported CSV leaves out its header row, so a downloaded file opens without column names. The local test export_header in tests/export.test.mjs fails on this (src/export.ts:31).
2. The export guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports only when clicked, so readers will wait for a file that never arrives. A corrected guide sentence is drafted (docs/export.md:8).

Reviewer maria pointed out the missing header in her PR comment (comment-73); the drafted reply agrees that the header is missing and says the fix is planned. The build check passed in CI, but the required unit check is still running, and the local test run failed on the header test. Two of the three points from your earlier review are now addressed. The branch was rebased onto main and pushed after one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved. One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the paging helper's code instead of calling it (src/export.ts:44), and deliver with nits can take it.

I recommend deliver because both problems have drafted repairs ready on your own PR.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair both problems, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code with the shared helper.
3. assess - post both problems to the PR as one review and make no repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved, and the functionality-only coverage is delivered in both the openings and A's evidence mapping, with no external observation or `not judged` outcome. Three After wordings came close to moving a fact and are worth tightening. First, standing in A is the nearest call: Before said the required unit check is still running "so merging also waits on it", while After only reports that the check is running next to the local failure, leaving the reader to infer from "required" that it precedes merge; restore an explicit clause such as "so merging also waits on it". Second, After's sync sentence adds "and pushed", which the supplied sync record does not state, and drops "no commits dropped"; keep the sentence to the supplied outcome (rebased onto main, one conflict in src/export.ts resolved, no commits dropped). Third, B's "You cannot approve your own PR." now stands as its own paragraph between standing and the recommendation, which strains the three-part shape; fold it back into the standing paragraph. Smaller risks: B dropped the supplied approval, the stop rows disagree ("remove the worktree" in A and C, "leave the worktree in place" in B), and C's assess row says "end at a closing menu", which reads as internal phrasing; Before's "end the run ... leave the PR as it is" was safer unless the skill mandates the cleanup wording.

Its small improvements are within facts that already held: A's second part now opens with a single standing sentence that names both the blockers and the running required check, and the inspection says "Commit being reviewed" where Before said "assessed head". Two things in A are worth tightening, though neither fails a fact: the test file path appears twice in blocker 1, and standing and problems run to several paragraphs, which strains the three-part shape.
